# ai-bunker

> A sovereign OpenAI-compatible gateway standing in front of your own GPU. It
> serves a versioned charter to every client, enforces rules that no client can
> bypass, and counts the context budget with the serving engine's own tokenizer
> instead of trusting the client's estimate.

Written for answer engines. Every figure below was measured; where a number is
an estimate, the project says so.

## The claim, in one paragraph

Gateways (LiteLLM, Kong, Portkey) route requests but do not inspect them: a tool
result full of secrets and a `rm -rf ~` pass through as ordinary bytes. Guardrail
libraries (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, LLM Guard) inspect content but are
libraries, so an agent that does not call them is unprotected. Neither counts the
context budget. ai-bunker occupies the intersection.

## Pages

- [ai-bunker — one GPU, one charter, every coding agent](https://deraison.ai/ai-bunker/): what it is, the four stages of a request, and what it deliberately is not.
- [Sizing](https://deraison.ai/ai-bunker/sizing.html): which machine to buy, from a memory-roofline model validated against published measurements.
- [Landscape](https://deraison.ai/ai-bunker/landscape.html): the gateways, the rule engines and the policy engines compared, including where this project is behind.
- [Get started](https://deraison.ai/ai-bunker/start.html): install, configure, serve, adopt a repository.

## Key facts

- **The session floor** is the part of a context window paid on every request and out of reach of compaction: system prompt, tool schemas, charter, knowledge index. What remains is the only room a conversation has.
- **Clients under-count their own tokens.** One measured session believed it was under 32,768 and sent 40,433; the server refused the whole request. Claude Code compacts at effective context minus a 13,000-token buffer — an estimate about an estimate.
- **A bloated floor loops silently.** One workstation had 59 locally-installed agent skills injected into every prompt: 17,754 tokens, 68% of a 26,226-token floor against a declared context of 26,000. Compaction fired on turn one with nothing to compact; the session returned 8 tokens per turn forever and the harness said nothing.
- **Decode speed is bounded by memory bandwidth divided by active weight bytes**, not by capacity. A DGX Spark has 128 GB and 273 GB/s, and serves a dense 24B coding model at 6.5 tokens/second.
- **Mixture-of-experts inverts the usual trade.** Qwen3-Coder-Next is 80B total and 3B active: the best open coding model in the catalogue is also the fastest to serve.
- **Rules ship with their own examples**, checked in CI. Three shipped patterns were wrong on first write; the examples caught all three.
- **The entropy threshold that tells a credential from a placeholder is 3.85 bits/character**, measured across ten common placeholders and six real-shaped credentials rather than guessed.

## Honest limits

- `0.1.0-alpha`. 354 tests and a green CI gate, but the public interface can still move.
- Command screening does not apply to streamed completions: a tool call arrives in fragments, and refusing it would mean buffering the whole response.
- The accessibility lint on the dashboard is static only; a browser audit catches what a rendered page reveals.
- Provider breadth is far behind LiteLLM. ai-bunker can sit in front of it rather than compete.
